text:
arjun: quick follow-up from the quant RFC — proposing we add tokenwise calibration metadata into the model artifact so runtime can correct low-bit output drift without full re-quantization
sofia: hm interesting. do you mean a lightweight per-token offset/scale we apply after logits? :thinking:
arjun: exactly. store small tables (per-vocab or per-subword bucket) with mean/std or a 2-param affine per-token that gets applied to logits before softmax
kevin: what's the expected size increase? storing per-token float32 for a 50k vocab could be big. we should consider quantizing the metadata too or bucketing tokens
tara: could we bucket by token-frequency or embedding-cluster instead of per-token? that would cut storage a lot
arjun: prototypes show 50k * 2 floats = ~400KB if float16, ~800KB float32. with 256 buckets we drop to ~4KB. so bucketing seems necessary for large vocabularies
sofia: runtime cost? adding an extra memory lookup and add per token could add tail latency on short requests
kevin: we can piggyback on KV cache lookup — metadata lookup can reuse the same access pattern. latency delta <1ms for common paths on our GPU pipeline
tara: security/privacy angle — if metadata is generated from customer prompts (calibration traces) we need to ensure it's not stored in shared manifests for hosted models
arjun: agreed. plan is: default model artifacts ship with calibration from eval corpora; customer-derived calibrations are private overlays stored as customer-scoped artifacts or passed at request time via header
kevin: interface options: (A) include in model manifest as "calibration_buckets": {..} (B) accept calibration overlay in request header x-rw-calib: base64(json) (C) reference by id in model config and fetched from private store
tara: B sounds flexible for enterprise private deployments but could bloat requests. C preferred for hosted with auth checks
sofia: we should also define fallback when bucket missing — fall back to identity transform and emit telemetry for coverage
arjun: yes. runtime semantics: apply if present, otherwise skip and emit metric quant.calib.miss with model+route tags
kevin: can we get away with int8 metadata to avoid extra memory traffic? store scale as uint8 + shared exponent? decode is cheap on host
ml-ci-bot: perf tests (dev clusters) — applying 256-bucket uint8 metadata adds +0.6ms median and +1.8ms p95 on text-gen microbench (seq len 32, batch 4)
sofia: thanks @ml-ci-bot. that seems reasonable for many workloads but we should gate on latency SLO per route before enabling globally
tara: operationally — need migration plan for Dedicated and Private. suggestion: add a new manifest version field "calib_v1" so older runtimes ignore it
arjun: proposal for next steps: 1) spec manifest schema snippet 2) perf experiments with bucket counts (64/256/1024) 3) privacy story + storage controls 4) runtime flag + telemetry. volunteers?
kevin: I can run perf matrix and add int8 encoding support
sofia: I'll draft the manifest schema and the privacy implications doc
tara: I'll write the runtime fallback + rollout playbook for ops
arjun: awesome — I'll collate and write a short RFC follow-up with examples. example manifest snippet:```
"calibration": {
  "version": "calib_v1",
  "scheme": "bucketed-uint8",
  "buckets": 256,
  "table_base64": "<base64-blob>",
  "bucket_map": "subword-cluster-256"
}
```
sofia: tiny nit — include checksum and encoding metadata (endianness) so different runtimes can validate
kevin: noted. also include a worst-case degrade flag that runtime can consult for strict SLO routes
tara: great. i'll sync with oncall later about emergency rollback steps :thumbsup:
ml-ci-bot: created perf job: rw/quant/calib/bucketed-256, ETA 3h
arjun: thanks all. i'll post the RFC follow-up later today and link tests here :)
